analysis.title: UBS House View - Daily US: Strengthen portfolio defenses as volatility rises
key_insights: UBS CIO says market volatility has risen over the past week as investors weigh AI profitability questions in a higher-rate environment while geopolitical conflicts remain unresolved. Brent crude was up 0.9% to nearly USD 110/bbl at the time of writing.

Q3 earnings season is in full swing and UBS expects further volatility. Markets are assessing hyperscalers' returns on AI investment, financing and execution risks in the AI buildout, and whether higher rates are weighing on business activity and consumer spending.

UBS still expects a robust reporting season, with AI-related growth helping drive S&P 500 earnings growth of 28%. Concentrated market performance and stock-specific volatility argue for portfolio resilience.

Structured strategies: put warrants for investors worried about a correction who want to keep equity exposure and limit losses on stocks they own. Capital preservation strategies for cautious adds, with participation in a recovery and protection of some or all of the initial investment at maturity. Reverse convertibles for income seekers where implied volatility is still elevated. Risks include issuer default, limited liquidity and capital loss.

Hedge funds may add differentiated returns as dispersion rises. Higher rates widen differences among companies, economies and securities, which may benefit equity market neutral strategies. Diverging central bank policies expand the opportunity set for discretionary macro, and uneven yield curve moves may help fixed income relative value.

Commodities can diversify portfolios and insulate against supply-driven inflation. Energy exposure may protect against supply disruptions. The longer-term outlook is supported by rising power demand, AI infrastructure investment, electrification and constrained supply, particularly copper. UBS favors diversified exposure across precious metals, energy, industrial metals and agriculture, actively managed.

UBS remains constructive on equities and recommends retaining diversified core exposure, while arguing the case for broadening sources of return has strengthened given concentrated leadership, higher financing costs and geopolitical risks.
UK CPI rose to 3.5% y/y in September from 3.1% in August, above the 3.4% consensus and the highest since October 2025. Services inflation rose to 3.7% from 3.4% and core to 2.8% from 2.6%.

UK labor data: regular pay growth edged up to 3.7% in the three months to August, payrolls rose 13,000 in September, and vacancies kept falling. Within the BoE MPC, Megan Greene stresses second-round effects of higher energy costs while Governor Bailey is more cautious on hikes.

UBS base case is a Bank of England hike in November, followed by another in Q1 2027 to 4.25%. Higher UK rates for longer could support sterling against the Swiss franc, consistent with UBS's GBPCHF carry-trade view. Next week's UK budget is a balancing act between supporting households and businesses and keeping confidence in public borrowing.

sector_views.rationale: Diversification, insulation against supply-driven inflation, and support from power demand, AI infrastructure, electrification and constrained copper supply.
